Report Details

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.953320, -87.937239 (Approximated from ZIP )
Reported Sheen Size: 8 feet by 1.5 miles (area 1.45 acres)
SkyTruth Minimum Estimate: 1.56 gallons
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** CUTTING OIL FROM A METAL SHAVINGS RECYCLE BIN LOCATED AT ADDISON MANUFACTURING IS BEING RELEASED FROM THE BIN ONTO CONCRETE. DURING A RAIN EVENT. THE OIL ENTERS THE STORM SEWER SYSTEM VIA OVERLAND FLOW. THE STORM SEWER SYSTEM OUTFALL IS AT A BOX CULVERT UNDER YORK ROAD JUST NORTH OF IRVING PARK ROAD IN BENSENVILLE INTO SILVER CREEK (I.E. BENSENVILLE DITCH). THE STORM WATER FLOWS THROUGH OHARE AIRPORT ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF THE AIRPORT PROPERTY. A HEAVY SHEEN WAS OBSERVED BY OHARE PERSONNEL ON TUESDAY, APRIL 16TH 2013. CHICAGO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT CONTRACTED SET ENVIRONMENTAL TO CONTAIN THE RELEASE, AND DETERMINE THE RESPONSIBLE PARTY. SET WORKED WITH THE VILLAGE OF BENSENVILLE TO TRACE THE RELEASE. OIL SAMPLES WERE COLLECTED FROM BEHIND THE CONTAINMENT BOOM AND AT ADDISON MANUFACTURING. THE ANALYTICAL RESULTS STATE THE OIL APPEARS TO BE FROM THE SAME SOURCE.

properties.title: NRC Report: Polychlorinated Biphenyls in Duck River near Columbia, TN
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 947969 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: GRAFTECH INTERNATIONAL HOLDINGS INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 947969
Incident Time: 2010-05-14 13:30:00
Nearest City: Columbia, TN
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: POLYCHLORINATED BIPHENYLS
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: GRAFTECH INTERNATIONAL HOLDINGS INC.
Skytruth Analysis
ON 5/1/10 AND 5/2/10, MIDDLE TENNESSEE EXPERIENCED ATYPICAL RAINFALL, OFTEN OCCURRING IN INTENSE BURSTS AND TOTALING 9.7 INCHES NEAR THE GRAFTECH MANUFACTURING SITE IN COLUMBIA. DUCK RIVER FLOODED AT A PEAK LEVEL OF 579.33 AMSL AND FLOW OF 45,000 CFS ALONG THE SITE BORDER. AFTER THE RIVER RECEDED, A BANK SLOPE FAILURE WAS DISCOVERED ON FRIDAY, 5/14/10, WHICH HAD DEPOSITED ABOUT 2,000 CF OF SOIL AND FILL MATERIAL INTO THE RIVER. GRAFTECH NOTIFIED TN DEC AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES AGENCY BY VOICE MAIL MESSAGES ON FRIDAY, 5/14/10. BOTH AGENCIES RESPONDED ON-SITE ON MONDAY, 5/17/10. THE ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS WAS ALSO NOTIFIED. GRAFTECH INSTALLED A TEMPORARY CHECK DAM AT THE BANK BREACH TO PREVENT ADDITIONAL MATERIALS FROM REACHING THE RIVER. REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLES WERE SUBSEQUENTLY TESTED FOR NUMEROUS PARAMETERS TO CHARACTERIZE THE RELEASED MATERIALS. THE MATERIALS WERE SURPRISINGLY FOUND TO CONTAIN 1.64 PPM PCBS, WHICH IS BELOW THE ESTABLISHED 5.3 PPM NOAA SEVERE EFFECT LEVEL FOR FRESHWATER SEDIMENT. THERE IS NO KNOWN OR ANTICIPATED SIGNIFICANT NEGATIVE IMPACT ON PUBLIC HEALTH, A DRINKING WATER RESOURCE, OR THE ENVIRONMENT. SURVEY ESTIMATED 2,000 CU. YDS. RELEASED. BASED ON THE MIXTURE RULE, THIS CONCENTRATION EQUATES TO APPROXIMATELY 8 LBS OF PCBS FOR THE TOTAL VOLUME OF MATERIALS RELEASED FROM THE RIVER BANK TO THE RIVER. GRAFTECH SUBMITTED A CORRECTIVE ACTION PLAN TO TN DEC AND THE ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS ON 7/12/10, WHICH IT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED UPON RECEIVING THEIR APPROVAL, TO SAFELY REMOVE AND DISPOSE OF THE DEPOSITED RIVER BANK MATERIALS.
